The prune follows the OOS row and DROPS it upstream, so the fixture never reaches the guard. Different sources = different blind spots. If anyone changes either layer's source, this row moves.

DELIBERATE TRADE, do not 'fix': stale feed still CONFIRMED 20:45, OOS refreshed to an UNCONFIRMED placeholder 15:00, now 16:00. The prune takes the time from OOS and the flag from the feed, so it DROPS a match that may not have started -- one run skips its refresh; the existing receipt stays and the next run restores it. The tempting fix (honour a confirmation only when its time matches the OOS row) flips stale_feed_fresh_oos__layers_differ to KEEP, so it reaches the guard, which trusts the stale 20:45 and refreshes after the real kick-off: a receipt BREACH. An omission recovers; a breach is permanent. Real defence: rebuild stage 3 straight after stage 2 so feed and OOS never diverge. (Proposed by the data analyst.)
